head: c9b66d93e9a08403392fe6813658e084d08876fc
summary: The runtime optimizations are sound and I found no weakened check, bypass or regression in the product code. Each reuse is scope-bounded and mutation-tested: withExecutableDigestObservation restores the prior observation in a finally, so no digest crosses an await, a throw or a separate observation (proven by lab-top5-identity.mjs and by validation-tree-delegate-binding.mjs, which now refuses an 'observation = previous' -> 'observation = new Map()' mutant); canonicalIdentityExecutableDigest memoizes on the full source text rather than on filesystem metadata, so identity-canonical-digest-memo.mjs's same-size, restored-mtime mutant is still rejected, separate roots stay fresh, and deletion still refuses; withVerificationPlanningObservation shares only the implementation digest across the synchronous initialPlans map, with independent recomputation at launch, completion and publication (planning-observation.test.mjs covers reuse, fresh calls, throwing scope, await and nested scope). The two reuses inside enforceAndStampEvidence (sharedIdentity when sharedExecution.effectiveTimeoutMs === effectiveTimeoutMs, and implementationDigest from beforeIdentity) replace a second read taken microseconds later in the same synchronous block with byte-identical inputs; both are declared as new RUNTIME_EVIDENCE_FACT_REGISTRY entries ('verification-executable-observation', 'verification-planning-observation', 'identity-canonical-digest-memo') and are required by verify-runtime-fact-contract.mjs, which now also executes the three new regressions. The parallel admissibility mutation workers preserve all 11 binding targets and 19 child outcomes on disjoint writable dist snapshots (top5-4-green-cache.log shows peakBindings 2, activeBindingsAtExit 0 and every binding child exiting non-zero), executeMutation restores the mutated file in a finally, the SIGKILL/timeout path still trips the result.signal === null assertion, and lab-top5-performance.mjs asserts the real repository dist hashes are unchanged. NODE_COMPILE_CACHE usage is per-run disposable and writes only under the pre-existing .proof-or-stop/runtime scratch location already used by this fixture; no validation PASS is cached. The imported review-intent-stage-cycle repair enforces at story_create (direct and from-draft), checklist_add, checklist_update and verification_intent_append plus the story_review consumer, is registered in process-fact-registry, pinned by verify-process-fact-contract.mjs, added to test:serial-reference and to full-suite RESOURCE_POLICY as isolated, and carries false-positive controls; its executable-pin escape hatch is explicitly enumerated and matched between the classifier regex and the registry rationale. The version bump is complete and consistent across package.json, package-lock.json, packages/main/package.json, packages/main/package-lock.json, packages/lab/package-lock.json, packages/utils/package-lock.json and PROOF_OR_STOP_CLI_VERSION, and exceptions.json plus identity-child-contract.json are rebound to the exact committed digests (I matched every rebound entry I read against the supplied per-file sha256 list). All REPORT.md percentages reproduce from the committed planning-before/after JSON and the RED/GREEN logs, and the recorded tool-owned run of lab-top5-cache-performance.mjs 5 at head exits 0 with TOP5_5_GREEN, PLANNING_SCAN_GREEN and the full runtime-fact contract. The failure is entirely in the release note. CHANGELOG.md points readers to release-combined-green.log, which does not exist (the committed artifact is logs/release-combined-green-rejected.log); it asserts a specific measured 0.3.358 candidate result (132.247 s heartbeat, 291.696 s fanout, 107.885 ms planning) that has no retained log or manifest digest, in the same entry that claims the logs are committed, and those numbers differ from the head-run measurements, confirming an unretained third run; and it files the newly landing review-intent-stage-cycle repair under a v0.3.351 heading even though review-gate-verification-intent.ts, reviewer-lane-names.ts, all four writer call sites and the test:review-gate-intent-cycle script are new files and new lines in this 0.3.359 commit, which misattributes a new blocking refusal to a release that does not contain it. A whitespace-only deletion in review-test-index-transition.ts also moves that file's raw source digest for no functional reason. Unverifiable dependencies, named rather than retried: packages/main/src/core/machine.ts and packages/main/src/handlers/acceptance-amendment.ts are not in the snapshot, so I could not confirm that the acceptance_amendment_propose/review/approve path cannot persist a verificationIntent outside the four guarded writers; scripts/identity-reviewed-source-data.json and scripts/verify-validation-static-edges.mjs are not supplied, so the exceptions.json duplicate-entry consolidation (one EX-0140 and one EX-0034 removed against unchanged sources) and the review-test-index-transition.ts digest move rest on the developer-supplied release-static-final.log reporting needsReview 0 with 330 exceptions rather than on my own re-run.

findings.problem: The inserted '## Lab review-intent-stage-cycle - v0.3.351 - 2026-09-13' entry attributes the review-intent-stage-cycle repair to release 0.3.351, but the repair's code first exists in this 0.3.359 commit: packages/main/src/core/review-gate-verification-intent.ts and packages/main/src/core/reviewer-lane-names.ts are new files (index 0000000000), and the four writer call sites (story_create direct and from-draft, checklist_add, checklist_update, verification_intent_append), the story_review consumer, the runtime:review_gate_intent_cycle_rejection registry entry and the test:review-gate-intent-cycle script are all added lines in this same diff. The entry's own heading convention is contradicted by the validation-top5-performance entry in the same commit, which states 'Release version is assigned by Lab Finish from the synchronized main baseline'. A reader or operator diffing behavior by CLI version would conclude that this new blocking refusal on story_create/checklist_add/checklist_update/verification_intent_append exists in 0.3.351 through 0.3.358, which it does not.
findings.fix: Move the review-intent-stage-cycle entry under the '## Lab validation-top5-performance - v0.3.359' release heading (or give it its own v0.3.359 heading), and state the originating host version separately, e.g. 'migrated from codex/lab-review-intent-stage-cycle, repair 82365ddd9d57bebd96617e58bfa054434de9e293, originally finished there at 0.3.351; first available locally in 0.3.359'.

findings.problem: The entry says 'That rejected attempt is retained in release-combined-green.log and is not passing release evidence.' No such file is committed. The retained artifact is docs/lab/validation-top5-performance/logs/release-combined-green-rejected.log, which is the name used correctly by REPORT.md and by manifest.json (sha256 a95be9605944782cfdac467abe4f07ba7f4285b9c611e28cc81495776f6b9d64, 2518 bytes). The release note therefore directs a reader to a nonexistent artifact for the one negative result it discloses.
findings.fix: Change 'release-combined-green.log' to 'docs/lab/validation-top5-performance/logs/release-combined-green-rejected.log' so the citation resolves to the committed, digest-covered artifact.

findings.problem: The paragraph 'The synchronized 0.3.358 candidate 6ab34f538c passed the unchanged combined GREEN command: native heartbeat 132.247 seconds ... native fanout 291.696 seconds ... one planning scan in 107.885 ms' asserts specific measured values with no retained log: manifest.json contains no entry for that run, and the numbers match none of the committed logs (planning-combined-lab-green.log records 130.737 s, planning-combined-planning-green.log records 308.174 s and 93.141 ms) nor the recorded head run (131.912 s, 294.609 s, 102.281 ms). This sits directly beside the claim that 'Original RED/GREEN logs, rejected candidates, a blocked quorum run, and SHA-256 manifests are committed under docs/lab/validation-top5-performance/', so the entry overstates its own evidence retention for this one measurement.
findings.fix: Either commit the 0.3.358 candidate log under docs/lab/validation-top5-performance/logs/ and add its sha256/bytes to manifest.json, or drop the specific numbers and state only that the candidate passed the unchanged combined GREEN command, marking that observation as not retained.

findings.problem: The only change to this file is deletion of a trailing blank line at end of file. It has no functional effect but does change the file's raw sha256, and no corresponding rebinding for this path appears anywhere in the diff (exceptions.json, identity-child-contract.json and ACTIVE_IDENTITY_EXECUTABLE_SOURCE_BINDINGS are all untouched for it). scripts/identity-reviewed-source-data.json is not in the supplied snapshot, so I cannot confirm from the provided inputs whether any pinned-source dataset binds this file's raw digest; if one does, the missing rebinding is a latent gate failure. Either way it is unexplained churn in a commit whose other source edits are all deliberate.
findings.fix: Restore the trailing newline so the file's raw digest is unchanged by this release, or, if the deletion is intentional, rebind it wherever review-test-index-transition.ts is pinned and say so in the release note.
